content:
I started using the new HTTP server available since 4.31.0 release of Lean 4.

I wanted to give some feedback to @Sofia Rodrigues

Overall Developper experience is great, i was able to implement a compile time Router on top of it without any surprise.
Kudos for the design. It's really polished.

If i have some improvements to add, it would not be directly on the HTTP side of it, but more on the Json side of things. Indeed, since Json as become the lingua franca of internet APIs, i think adding small Request and Response helpers could be awesome to help serialize and deserialize in one liners.

Here is some helpers i used that could be great to add in the library :

namespace Std.Http.Response
def json [ToJson α] (j : α) : ContextAsync (Response Body.Any) :=
  Response.ok |>.json <| Json.pretty <| toJson j

def json.created [ToJson α] (j : α) : ContextAsync (Response Body.Any) :=
  Response.created |>.json <| Json.pretty <| toJson j

end Std.Http.Response

namespace Std.Http.Request

def parseJson (req : Request Body.Stream) {α : Type} [FromJson α] : ContextAsync (Except String α) := do
  let body : String ← Body.Stream.readAll req.body
  return (Lean.Json.parse body >>= fromJson? (α := α))

end Std.Http.Request

And here you can see an example of a router i'm working on (just for showing that we can now build great APIs framework on top of Std.HTTP.

Router Library example

import Leanio.Router
open Std Async
open Std Http Server
open Leanio.Router
open Lean
open Std
set_option linter.unusedVariables false
-- ==========================================
-- Data structures
-- ==========================================
structure Todo where
  id        : Nat
  title     : String
  completed : Bool
  userId    : Nat
deriving ToJson

structure CreateTodoRequest where
  title  : String
  userId : Nat
deriving FromJson

structure UpdateTodoRequest where
  title?     : Option String := none
  completed? : Option Bool := none
  userId?    : Option Nat := none
deriving FromJson

namespace Todo

def ofCreateTodo (todo: CreateTodoRequest) (id: Nat) (completed: Bool): Todo :=
 { id, completed, title := todo.title, userId := todo.userId }

def ofUpdateTodo (upd: UpdateTodoRequest) (todo: Todo) : Todo :=
 { todo with
   title     := upd.title?      |>.getD todo.title
   completed  := upd.completed? |>.getD todo.completed
   userId     := upd.userId?    |>.getD todo.userId
 }

end Todo

structure TodoStore where
  todos      : HashMap Nat Todo
  nextTodoId : Nat

structure TodoStoreRef where
  ref : IO.Ref TodoStore
deriving TypeName

structure APIError where
  error   : String
  message : String
deriving ToJson, FromJson

-- ==========================================
-- JSON helpers
-- ==========================================
namespace Std.Http.Response

def json [ToJson α] (j : α) : ContextAsync (Response Body.Any) :=
  Response.ok |>.json <| Json.pretty <| toJson j

def json.created [ToJson α] (j : α) : ContextAsync (Response Body.Any) :=
  Response.created |>.json <| Json.pretty <| toJson j

def json.badRequest (msg : String) : ContextAsync (Response Body.Any) :=
  Response.badRequest |>.json (Json.pretty (toJson (APIError.mk "Bad Request" msg)))

def json.notFound (msg : String) : ContextAsync (Response Body.Any) :=
  Response.notFound |>.json (Json.pretty (toJson (APIError.mk "Not Found" msg)))

end Std.Http.Response

namespace Std.Http.Request

def parseJson (req : Request Body.Stream) {α : Type} [FromJson α] : ContextAsync (Except String α) := do
  let body : String ← Body.Stream.readAll req.body
  return (Lean.Json.parse body >>= fromJson? (α := α))

end Std.Http.Request

-- ==========================================
-- State helpers
-- ==========================================

def noTodoState : ContextAsync (Response Body.Any) :=
  Response.internalServerError |>.json (Json.pretty (toJson (APIError.mk "Internal Server Error" "todo state middleware not installed")))

def withTodoState (req : Request Body.Stream) (f : IO.Ref TodoStore → ContextAsync (Response Body.Any)) : ContextAsync (Response Body.Any) :=
  match req.extensions.get TodoStoreRef with
  | some wrapper => do
    f wrapper.ref
  | none => noTodoState

-- ==========================================
-- Todo Routes
-- ==========================================

GET "/todos" listTodos (req : Request Body.Stream) :=
  withTodoState req fun ref => do
    let store ← ref.get
    Response.json store.todos.valuesArray

GET "/todos/{id}" getTodoById (req : Request Body.Stream) (id : Nat) :=
  withTodoState req fun ref => do
    match (←ref.get).todos.get? id with
    | some todo => Response.json todo
    | none      => Response.json.notFound s!"Todo {id} not found"

POST "/todos" createTodo (req : Request Body.Stream) := do
  let .ok r  ← req.parseJson | Response.json.badRequest "invalid request todo body"
  withTodoState req fun ref => do
    let store ← ref.get
    let newId := store.nextTodoId
    let todo := Todo.ofCreateTodo r newId false
    ref.set { store with todos := store.todos.insert newId todo, nextTodoId := newId + 1 }
    Response.json.created todo

PUT "/todos/{id}" updateTodo (req : Request Body.Stream) (id : Nat) := do
  let .ok upd ← req.parseJson | Response.json.badRequest "invalid request todo body"
  withTodoState req fun ref => do
    let store ← ref.get
    match store.todos.get? id with
    | none => Response.json.notFound s!"Todo {id} not found"
    | some todo =>
      let updated := todo.ofUpdateTodo upd
      ref.set { store with todos := store.todos.insert id updated }
      Response.json updated

DELETE "/todos/{id}" deleteTodo (req : Request Body.Stream) (id : Nat) :=
  withTodoState req fun ref => do
    let store ← ref.get
    match store.todos.get? id with
    | some _ =>
      ref.set { store with todos := store.todos.erase id }
      Response.ok |>.text s!"Todo {id} deleted"
    | none => Response.json.notFound s!"Todo {id} not found"

-- ==========================================
-- Router construction
-- ==========================================
def todosRouter : Router := Router.empty
  |>.addRoute listTodos
  |>.addRoute getTodoById
  |>.addRoute createTodo
  |>.addRoute updateTodo
  |>.addRoute deleteTodo

def rootRouter : Router := Router.empty
  |>.addRouter "/api/v1" todosRouter
  |>.addMiddleware loggingMiddleware

-- ==========================================
-- Entry point
-- ==========================================

def main : IO Unit := Async.block do
  let addr : Net.SocketAddress := .v4 ⟨.ofParts 127 0 0 1, 8080⟩
  let todoRef ← IO.mkRef { todos := ∅, nextTodoId := 1 : TodoStore }
  let todoWrapper := { ref := todoRef : TodoStoreRef }
  let router := rootRouter
    |> Router.addMiddleware (withState TodoStoreRef todoWrapper)
  let server ← Server.serve addr router
  IO.println "Listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080"
  server.waitShutdown
And the Router API with compile time elaborator is just 250 lines of code.

Hi! I'm really glad we're getting a Http server. I hope it's okay if I open a thread for random bits of feedback on it.

First off, I get a very good first vibe from it. I am very glad there is a tutorial-y doc comment in Std/Http.lean. So I went and started copy-pasting some examples to play around with.

The hello world works out of the box. I can even #eval main and it will indeed host a server on localhost:8080. Nice. Although... it fails to shut down. I know doing this is probably not the intended way of using Http, hence I shouldn't complain.

The second example from Std/Http.lean fails to compile (Lean 4.31.0):

import Std.Http
open Std Async Http

def handler (req : Request Body.Stream) : ContextAsync (Response Body.Stream) := do
  let method := req.head.method -- error: Invalid field notation: Function `Request.head` does not have a usable parameter of type `Request ...` for which to substitute `req`
  ...

Is it welcome/useful if I (and others) post more spontaneous feedback?
I got into the exact same issue, use req.line.method instead.
forgot to mention it on my feedback
And maybe we could merge our feedbacks together to evoid searching through different threads
Ah, I thought your thread was about a specific thing, so I did not want to hijack it. Sure, we can merge them.

Thank you both for the feedback. The mini-tutorial which is currently part of the code will hopefully move soon to a proper place where it is easier to discover and checked by Verso to compile on the current Lean version.

As for JSON, the current Lean.Json is something that grew out of our own needs when implementing Lean, and was never really designed as a public API (though we don't oppose using it). Within the next year, there are plans to create a Std.Json that is really designed as a public API and well-integrated with the rest of the standard library.

This is the convention we have in our naming convention (https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/blob/master/doc/std/naming.md#acronyms):

For acronyms which are three letters or shorter, all letters should use the same case as dictated by the convention. For example, IO is a correct name for a type and the name IO.Ref may become IORef when used as part of a definition name and ioRef when used as part of a theorem name.

For acronyms which are at least four letters long, switch to lower case starting from the second letter. For example, Json is a correct name for a type, as is JsonRPC.

If an acronym is typically spelled using mixed case, this mixed spelling may be used in identifiers (for example Std.Net.IPv4Addr).
StateCpsT? I guess a condition is that nothing follows the acronym
That one precedes the introduction of the naming convention and hasn't been renamed yet.

By the way, my favorite example of a corner case for this is docs#MeasureTheory.L1.SimpleFunc.setToL1SCLM (which is correct according to the convention, although the convention doesn't apply to it). To assess whether the name is correct, you need to know that L1S and CLM are separate acronyms.
I'm sure there is a joke to be made about German compound words here.

Another feedback.

Currently, Query is under the URI namespace. I think it should be put out of it.
Indeed, i've added support for "application/www-url-encoded" in LeanIO and it's format and then structure is the same as URI.Query by definition.
So for now i haveURI.Query in my code when it's really not about URI, but body content. So relocating it to just Query namespace would be nice.

Another one related is that the parser (URI.Query.parseQuery) is private. For this one just removing the private attribute would also be nice.
It would allow me to just use it. For now, i just copy pasted it.
